text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 6.4px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #3b9c6e

g.text: CHAPTER 20 · ON ONE PAGE

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2430

g.text: The bake-off: six ways to make a decision

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2430

g.text: Six contestants, one fair test
Each was trained or tuned on three weeks of Kestrel
alerts (14,973) and scored on the fourth (5,027), on
ranking, calibration, cost, speed, stability and
labels needed.
Logistic regression
Jev (mock)
Text classifier
LLM-as-judge
LLM, JSON
Rules

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2430

g.text: Where Jev loses
With enough labels and clean fields, logistic
regression matches or beats it: AUC 0.896 against
0.892, at almost no cost per decision. Rules win on
explainability. Nothing is cheaper than a rule.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2430

g.text: Where it wins
No labels to start, typed answers that always parse,
and probabilities that rank and are close to
calibrated. It reads raw text better than a bag-of-
words classifier.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2430

g.text: The LLM’s real problem
Stated confidences snap to a few values, so they
can’t rank. 3.2% of JSON answers broke. At
temperature 0.7, 5.2% of verdicts changed on a second
ask.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2430

g.text: Read the design, not the winner
The mock LLM was built as a noisier reader than mock
Jev. The accuracy gap between them is a design
choice, not a finding. Run this contest on your own
data.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.2px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2430

g.text: The scorecard has eight columns
Pick the method that wins on the columns your
decision cares about. Often that’s two methods
together.

text.style: font-weight: 600; font-size: 7.2px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #1f2430

g.text: Next: turning probabilities into act, review and escalate.
